To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) multi-task learning can be beneficial for many computer vision applications, 2) multi-task learning should be used with care, 3) the tasks that are learned simultaneously should be chosen with care, and 4) the tasks that compete should not be computed by the same network.

(a) the tasks should be learned together if they cooperate with each other, (b) the tasks should not be learned in the same network if they compete, and (c) a multi-task neural network is better than many single-task networks in terms of inference time and accuracy.

(i) the performance of a multi-task network depends on the cooperation and competition of tasks, (ii) task cooperation can be increased by grouping tasks with similar objectives and task competition can be decreased by grouping tasks with different objectives, (iii) the number of neural networks can be decreased by assigning groups of tasks to the same network, and (iv) our approach can improve performance and decrease the inference time of multi-task neural networks
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) What is the impact of task cooperation and competition on multi-task neural network performance? (ii) How should tasks be assigned to a few networks to maximize performance?

the answer to the question 'which tasks should be learned together in multi-task learning?' depends on the specific task and the specific dataset.

multi-task learning is a powerful tool, but only when tasks are properly assigned to neural networks.

task cooperation and competition can be exploited in multi-task learning to improve performance.
the task cooperation-competition relationship is a crucial factor for the success of multi-task learning.
multi-task learning is a powerful paradigm that can lead to better performance when tasks are assigned carefully.
